description: Understanding platforms and methods for identifying, integrating, and assessing the suitability of internal, external, and alternative digital data assets relevant to program objectives.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.'
change to work: The scope expands beyond survey operations to active leadership of digital needs analysis, alternative data discovery, and digital resource prioritization. The Assistant Director will need to govern processes ensuring digital/automated alternatives are evaluated using standardized frameworks before directing sub-divisional programs.
justification: There is no explicit requirement in the current work-description for expertise in digital data discovery or assessment frameworks.

description: Ability to evaluate statistical programs for automation suitability, and oversee structured approaches for integrating automation solutions wherever possible.
historic work: Key Activities: 'Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.'
change to work: The scope expands beyond survey operations to active leadership of digital needs analysis, alternative data discovery, and digital resource prioritization. The Assistant Director will need to govern processes ensuring digital/automated alternatives are evaluated using standardized frameworks before directing sub-divisional programs.
justification: Current description lacks reference to automation readiness and feasibility assessment as core operational priorities.

development area: Cost-Benefit and Tradeoff Analysis in Digital Context
description: Capability to weigh cost, timeliness, quality, and strategic alignment of digital/automated solutions versus traditional survey initiation.
historic work: Technical Activities: Decision Making - 'Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives. Approves survey content and design...Directs the conduct of in-depth and unique surveys in an area of specialization...Defends proposals for the development of new surveys.'
change to work: Decision-making must shift to explicitly require a digital-first pre-assessment prior to recommendation/approval of surveys. The Assistant Director must be able to interpret comprehensive digital/alternative data asset evaluations and cost-benefit tradeoff analysis as a mandatory precursor to any new survey proposal.
justification: No mention of cost-benefit analysis or digital-asset pre-screening in current survey approval process.

development area: Enterprise Data Asset Reuse & Digital Feasibility Planning
description: Ability to identify, plan for, and allocate resources towards projects based on their digital integration options, reusability of existing data resources, and technology scalability.
historic work: Technical Activities: Leadership and Operational Management - 'Develops long term plans and objectives and allocates human resources requirements...Plans, develops and manages budgets for projects... negotiates and approves contracts... Selects contractors for specific projects, assigns, directs, manages and evaluates the work according to contract specifications.'
change to work: Resource and budget planning must now emphasize enterprise-wide data asset reuse, digital feasibility prioritization, and multilateral project integration. Contracts and long-term plans should reflect prioritization of digital solutions and cross-program synergy.
justification: No current explicit skill or knowledge requirement for multi-source asset management or digital cross-program feasibility analysis.

development area: Digital Feasibility Communication & Business Case Defense
description: Ability to clearly articulate findings from digital/alternative data asset assessments, automation readiness analyses, and to defend survey or project proposals based on thorough digital-first logic.
historic work: Technical Activities: Communication - 'Defends proposals for the development of new surveys to address current socio-economic trends...Presents arguments and options and negotiates resources and timeframes...Chairs intra-departmental meetings...participates in inter-departmental meetings, conferences...to develop consensus...'
change to work: The defense and presentation of new survey proposals must now be underpinned by formal evidence of digital asset/automation option exhaustion and robust cost/time/resource tradeoff justifications, requiring new forms of communication competence.
justification: No explicit communication requirements regarding digital data feasibility findings or automation-first rationale are present.

description: Ability to systematically identify, evaluate, and synthesize machine-actionable metadata across diverse data assets using automated platforms.
historic work: Key Activities: Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
change to work: The scope of direction will now integrate rigorous asset evaluation and transparent, evidence-driven justification for new initiatives, with increased use of asset evaluation technology.
justification: The future role requires up-to-date competency with asset-centric data review and automated asset evaluation platforms, not currently emphasized.

development area: Cost-benefit & Feasibility Analysis in Asset Reuse
description: Ability to evaluate, present, and negotiate the comparative value, potential reusability, and feasibility of existing versus new data assets.
historic work: Technical Activities: 1. change to work: Decision-making shifts from survey-first solutions to using systematic reviews of data assets as the default, and defending new surveys only with evidence-based, asset-gap-driven rationale.
justification: Skill in evaluating cost-benefit, feasibility, and reuse for data assets during rapid consultation cycles will be newly essential.

justification: Familiarity with tools supporting transparent, efficient stakeholder engagement on asset-centric analysis is not addressed in the current description.

description: Ability to lead negotiations with a clear focus on evidence from asset reviews, cost-benefit and reuse potential, communicating complex trade-offs quickly and with transparency.
historic work: Technical Activities: 3. Communication: Mediates ... to establish joint survey agreements, ... to monitor relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results.
change to work: Communications will shift toward outcome- and evidence-focused negotiation on data reuse and asset leverage, making transparent rationale for new data collection explicit in all dialogues.

change to work: Research and analysis will increasingly require the integration of systematic asset analysis to justify or reject the pursuit of new surveys, reflecting asset-centric evidence in all proposals.
justification: Expertise in synthesizing machine-actionable metadata into research analysis is not highlighted in the current work-description.

description: Understanding automation strategies, capabilities, and frameworks as applied to statistical operations to evaluate and implement automation opportunities.
historic work: Key Activities - Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
change to work: The scope of 'statistical program operations' and analysis must now include digital optimization, automation-readiness assessments, and maximizing data asset reuse. Supervision and direction must embed considerations of how workflows can be digitized and automated, not just executed efficiently in traditional terms.
justification: The shift to a data ecosystem optimization model requires knowledge of automated processes and digital workflows. Existing description does not specify digital-first or automation-readiness leadership.

description: Ability to lead teams in re-designing program operations for automation, digital data integration, and machine-actionable workflows.
historic work: Key Activities - Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
change to work: The scope of 'statistical program operations' and analysis must now include digital optimization, automation-readiness assessments, and maximizing data asset reuse. Supervision and direction must embed considerations of how workflows can be digitized and automated, not just executed efficiently in traditional terms.
justification: Approvals now explicitly require digital workflow and interoperability considerations, missing from current leadership duties.

description: Ability to construct and evaluate formal business cases that weigh automation, interoperability, and cost-savings against manual/survey options under enterprise digital priorities.
historic work: Technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts - 1. Decision making - Reviews strategic directions for surveys, recommends solutions to achieve goals, approves content/design, data integration, recommends objectives/content, defends new surveys, negotiates funding.
change to work: Decision-making must now start with assessment of all potential automated, interoperable, or reusable data options before defaulting to manual or new survey solutions. Objective-setting, approvals, and funding justifications must be grounded in agency-level cost-benefit cases under digital execution expectations.
justification: Cost/benefit analysis must pivot from basic survey justifications to include automation, reuse, IT integration, and digital delivery impacts.

description: Comprehensive understanding of agency and external data ecosystems, interoperability standards, and practical evaluation of reuse and data blending potential.

change to work: Decision-making must now start with assessment of all potential automated, interoperable, or reusable data options before defaulting to manual or new survey solutions. Objective-setting, approvals, and funding justifications must be grounded in agency-level cost-benefit cases under digital execution expectations.
justification: Explicit requirement for knowledge of digital data integration and interoperability is new.

description: Awareness of what skills, contracts, technologies, and planning are involved in setting up digital-first and automated statistical operations.
historic work: Technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts - 2. Leadership and operational management - Develops plans/objectives/allocates resources, directs recruitment, manages budgets, negotiates contracts.
change to work: Long-term plans, project objectives, recruitment, and budget management now include explicit requirements for automation/digital readiness, with human and financial resource considerations favoring scalable and interoperable solutions.
justification: Planning and operational management must now reflect digital/automation-build expertise.

description: Ability to assess suitability, legality, and machine-actionability of digital and automated external/internal data in program design and approval.
historic work: Technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts - 6. Research and analysis - Analyzes trends, user needs, develops proposals, reviews/approves analytical materials.
change to work: Analysis must now include critical evaluation of automated and reusable digital data sources as first-line options, so that proposals for new collection use survey/manual workflows only as a last resort—requiring robust supporting evidence and a detailed value case.
justification: Analytical and research skills expand to encompass evaluation of digital and automated data asset quality, suitability, and operational feasibility.

description: The ability to interpret, analyze, and validate machine-derived concepts and metadata within enterprise-wide digital systems.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts | 1. Decision making | 'Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations...'
change to work: Approval of survey content and design will be heavily informed by machine-suggested concepts, requiring validation and exception handling rather than creation. Decision-making processes will involve evaluating machine-generated options and advocating for standardized use, with well-documented justification required for departures from enterprise standards.
justification: Current skills focus on manual approval and expert assessment of concepts; however, the future role requires technical fluency in assessing AI-generated metadata and digital traceability.

description: Skill in articulating, defending, and negotiating the rationale for choices around concept alignment, especially in enterprise-wide standardization discussions.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts | 1. Decision making | 'Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations...'
change to work: Approval of survey content and design will be heavily informed by machine-suggested concepts, requiring validation and exception handling rather than creation. Decision-making processes will involve evaluating machine-generated options and advocating for standardized use, with well-documented justification required for departures from enterprise standards.
justification: Future task demands require justifying departures from AI-suggested concepts to multiple stakeholders and within governance boards.

description: Competency in mediating and resolving disagreements quickly among stakeholders with respect to machine-suggested standards and data concepts.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts | 3. Communication | 'Mediates with senior executives of major Canadian corporations... to monitor relevant concepts and practices related to the use and application of program results.'

justification: The transition to rapid, tech-enabled arbitration will require advanced facilitation and conflict resolution skills in digital and cross-disciplinary contexts.

description: Understanding of how statistical concepts and metadata are embedded, aligned, and governed across digital architectures and platforms.

change to work: Knowledge expectations expand from subject-matter expertise to include an understanding of enterprise digital architectures and digital governance processes for statistical concepts.
justification: Fulfilling the future responsibility of integrating statistic program concepts within digital ecosystems requires knowledge of digital platform integration.

description: Skill in critically appraising and providing quality assurance on AI-driven concept generation and its integration within research programs.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts | 6. Research and analysis | 'Directs the development of new methods and techniques for unique studies, assesses the implications of new approaches and develops solutions to complex issues.'
change to work: Research and analysis work will increasingly involve evaluating the validity, reliability, and practical impact of machine-suggested concepts and methodologies, rather than creating new concepts directly.
justification: Gap exists in the ability to critically assess the suitability and implications of AI-driven conceptual frameworks within statistical research.

description: Ability to interpret, monitor, and troubleshoot software that scans existing/alternative data sources and provides evidence-based recommendations on survey necessity.
historic work: Key Activities: Directs, through subordinates, the work of a sub-division involved in statistical program operations, analysis, interpretation, marketing and dissemination.
change to work: The sub-division's focus shifts from routine survey operations to managing technology-enabled data source evaluation, automated data integration, and negotiating rare, high-stakes survey undertakings. Day-to-day work increasingly revolves around overseeing processes and technologies that exhaustively scan data sources and only signal survey needs when fully justified.
justification: Skill shift required as automated systems drive data source evaluation; understanding underlying logic and outputs is necessary to direct subordinates effectively.

change to work: The sub-division's focus shifts from routine survey operations to managing technology-enabled data source evaluation, automated data integration, and negotiating rare, high-stakes survey undertakings. Day-to-day work increasingly revolves around overseeing processes and technologies that exhaustively scan data sources and only signal survey needs when fully justified.
justification: Leadership must transition from operational management of survey cycles to complex oversight of automated data vetting and multidisciplinary teams.

development area: Interpretation of Machine-Actionable Metadata and Suitability Logic
description: Ability to understand the rules and logic underpinning data source suitability determination, and translate outputs to actionable recommendations.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 1. Decision making: Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives. Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.

Strategic contribution becomes less about survey optimization and more about legal/ethical review and technology oversight.
justification: Ability to interpret technical outputs of automated systems and explain rationale to non-technical stakeholders.

description: Advanced negotiation skills for securing access to alternative administrative and private sector data sources in complex legal/ethical contexts.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 1. Decision making: Defends proposals for the development of new surveys and negotiates the allocation of funding for the conduct of projects.
change to work: Defending survey launches now requires transparent, auditable evidence based on automated output. Negotiations with funding bodies and data sources are higher-stakes, focusing on the exceptional nature of new surveys and emphasizing the exhaustion of alternative data options.
justification: Exceptional negotiation skills required for multi-party, potentially contentious discussions with data holders and partners.

development area: Data Sharing Agreements and Privacy Law
description: Understanding of the legislative and regulatory environment affecting data sharing, automated source scans, privacy preservation, and the negotiation of data access agreements.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Expert knowledge of advanced economic or sociology theories and principles relating to a specialized subject area ... to define the objectives, content and approaches of unique and complex analytical projects covering a broad area of specialization or a range of departmental statistical programs...
change to work: While substantive expertise remains important, there is new demand for understanding metadata frameworks, technological evaluations, and applicable legal frameworks related to data reuse, privacy, and data sharing.

development area: Evaluation of Automated Data Availability Assessments
description: Ability to critically assess the outcomes of automated data discovery and suitability tools, ensuring their sufficiency to rule out or justify new collection.
historic work: Technical Activities, Skills, Responsibilities, or Efforts: 6. Research and analysis: Analyses user needs in relation to current socio-economic trends and developments at the national and international levels, translates them into a concrete, timely and affordable information request, determines the implications of proposed areas of study and defends proposals for the development of new surveys.
change to work: Analysis increasingly centers on matching user needs to findings from automated scans, and only proposing new surveys once algorithmic checks are exhausted and documented. Justifications are technical and evidence-backed, not solely expert- or stakeholder-driven.
justification: Analytical work pivots to interpreting system outputs and evaluating whether a new data collection is justified.

description: Understanding of automation technologies, the principles behind automation-first business case construction, and recognition of modular/stateless process value.
historic work: technical activities, skills, responsibilities, or efforts > 1. Decision making > Reviews strategic directions for the management of significant surveys and recommends innovative solutions to address departmental goals and objectives. Approves survey content and design; sample estimation and imputation methods; data integration from different sources; sample sizes and allocations to maximize efficiency within resource constraints.
change to work: This element must be updated so the EC-08 role explicitly reviews and champions automation-first and modular solutions, prioritizes non-survey data sources and enterprise data integration, and foregrounds empirical justification for approaches. Decision-making now emphasizes discontinuing or iterating non-performing projects and platform alignment, rather than only optimizing survey design.
justification: Current description does not reference automation-first strategy, modular approaches, or explicit cost-benefit evidence as central to recommendations.
